title: Sale Ad Creatives for Discounts and Promos | AIVideosUGC
description: Make sale ad creatives from your product photos: banners with open space for your offer and short promo clips. Add the price yourself and get your sale live.
h1: Sale Ad Creatives With Room for Your Offer
lead: Get sale ad creatives with clean visuals for your next markdown and a clear spot left for the percentage off, the code and the end date you add yourself.
card: Clean visuals with room for the percentage off, the code and the end date.
intro: A sale ad has one job: get people to notice the deal and tap. That means the product should be easy to recognize, and there should be a clean area where the offer can sit without fighting the background.

AIVideosUGC makes the visual part. Choose a square image with your product on one side and open space on the other, or a short promo clip in 9:16 or 1:1. The numbers, like the amount off, a code or "ends Sunday," get added in Canva, CapCut or Ads Manager. That keeps AI typos off your ads, and the same visual is ready to use again for the next sale.

ideas.d: Your product on one side and a plain, colored area on the other, ready for the offer text.
Two or three products grouped together for a buy-more-save-more offer.
A quick vertical clip of the product turning in the light, with space at the top for the discount you add in CapCut.
A new scene for the final days of the sale, so people who saw your first ad notice something different.

plan.d: Choose the products going on sale, refresh their main photos, and decide which channels the sale will run on.
Make the banners and clips in each size you need, add the offer text, and prepare a separate version for the final days.
Switch to the last-chance version near the end, and take down any visuals that show the discount once the sale is over.

faq.q: Can AIVideosUGC put the discount on the image for me?
faq.a: We leave the offer off on purpose. AI can garble words and numbers, so type the percentage and code yourself in Ads Manager, CapCut or Canva and check every character.

faq.q: Can I reuse a sale visual for my next promotion?
faq.a: Yes. Since the price isn't part of the image, the same background works again. Swap the text layer and it's ready.

faq.q: Can I show the original price next to the sale price?
faq.a: Only show an original price you actually charged. Many places have advertising rules about comparison pricing, so check what applies where you sell.

faq.q: What size should a sale ad use on social media?
faq.a: Use 9:16 for Stories and Reels, 1:1 for feed placements, and 16:9 for wide placements. Add the exact sale price and code after download.

overview.h2: Build the scene first and the offer second
overview.d: A discount creative has two separate layers. The scene must identify the product and make the frame easy to scan; the offer layer must contain the exact percentage, code, date, and conditions. Leave a deliberate quiet area in the generated image or video, then type the deal yourself after download. When the offer changes, you can update the text without rebuilding the visual.

overview.h2: Make each sale version answer a different question
overview.d: Use a clean square image when the feed needs a fast product read, a 9:16 clip when the sale is phone-first, and a 16:9 composition when the same visual belongs on a wide page; 4:3 and 3:4 are also available. AIVideosUGC offers 6, 10, 15, and 30 second jobs and shows their credit cost before generation. A second version can change the product action or camera angle; it should not invent a new discount.

input_guide.h2: Prepare a sale source that leaves usable space

items.d: Use a photo where the item is recognizable at a glance and its most important feature faces the camera.
Describe the product on the left or right of a calm surface, wall, or color field so your editor has room for the offer.

items.t: Keep the code out of the scene
items.d: Do not ask AI to render the discount code, price, or end date. Place those as editable text after download.

results.h2: A sale asset ready for an accurate offer

items.d: The item remains visible even after you place the discount headline beside it.
A clean area gives your editor room to set hierarchy without covering the product.
A scene without an embedded date can support another promotion after the text layer is replaced.

after_download.h2: Add the promotion with exact wording

items.d: Add the percentage, code, original price, sale price, and end date in Canva, CapCut, or Ads Manager, then proofread each one.
Only show an original price you actually charged and review the pricing rules that apply where you sell.
Make sure the product and the offer remain readable in the feed, Story, or ad preview before spending budget.
Take down old dates and codes when the promotion ends, even if the underlying scene remains useful.

good: Single products with an obvious visual identity
Bundles whose contents can be checked against a real inventory
Sales where the price or end date may change
Teams that want a clean base visual and a separate text layer
not_ideal: Promotions that depend on AI spelling a code correctly
Comparison-price claims without a verified original price
